evals.description: Entities accumulate correctly across sessions: each act invocation appends new entity entries to entities.mem without overwriting previous ones.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/inbox && echo "0/2 | not-started" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/progress && printf "+step:id=1,text=create-user-service,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=create-order-service,atomic=true
" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/steps.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/entities.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/stale.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-3/user-service.ts /tmp/eval-act-3/order-service.ts
evals.expected_output: After both steps are acted on, entities.mem contains entries for both UserService and OrderService. The first entity entry is not overwritten when the second is appended.

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/entities.mem contains at least two distinct entity entries after both steps execute
The entity entry recorded during step 1 still exists in entities.mem after step 2 runs

evals.description: Entity dedup: same entity must not be appended twice. Re-running act on the same step should not create duplicate entity entries.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/inbox && echo "1/2 | create-user-service" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/progress && printf "+step:id=1,text=create-user-service,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=create-order-service,atomic=true
" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/steps.mem && printf "+entity:name=UserService,kind=class,file=user-service.ts
" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/memory/entities.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-4/.memplan/stale.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-4/user-service.ts
evals.expected_output: entities.mem still contains exactly one UserService entry after the run.

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/entities.mem contains exactly one entry for UserService after the skill runs
The skill explicitly checks for existing entity entries before appending (output or behaviour confirms dedup)

evals.prompt: Act on step 3, but it fails during execution.
evals.description: Failure recording: when a step fails the skill must write a +failure: entry with cmd and reason fields to failures.mem.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/inbox && echo "2/3 | ran-migrations" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/progress && printf "+step:id=1,text=init-db,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=seed-db,deps=1,atomic=true
+step:id=3,text=run-integration-tests,deps=2,atomic=true
" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/steps.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/memory/entities.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-5/.memplan/stale.mem
evals.expected_output: failures.mem gets a +failure: entry containing a cmd field (the command that failed) and a reason field (the error message or exit code).

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/failures.mem contains a +failure: entry after the failed step
The +failure: entry includes a cmd= field identifying what was run
The +failure: entry includes a reason= field describing why it failed
